sentences.text: 1 This claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .9,05,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief:-
On 03.07.2022 at about 09.05 a.m., the petitioner was going in his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-05- LB-6035 in order to meet his friends and when he reached near Singasandra Bus Stand, Hosur Main Road from Electronic City to Kudlu Gate Junction, a Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-04-B-4346, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to him.
Due to the accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter, petitioner was shifted to Kauvery Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent huge amount towards medicines, attendant, conveyance and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working at Broad Com Company at Wipro Campus, Electronic City, Bengaluru as a Technician and earning a sum of .1,10,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Canter by its driver.
The respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of service of notice, the respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
Respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.1 has also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further, respondent No.1 contended that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.

The respondent No.2, being the owner and knowing that the driver was under intoxicated state, allowed the vehicle to be driven by him at public place and as such, violated the terms of the policy as well as M.V rules.
The police have inserted relevant provision in the final report in that regard and as such, respondent No.1 is not liable to indemnify respondent No.2 as there is violation of terms of policy.
The petitioner was also negligent and he was driving the vehicle without valid and effective licence at the time of accident.
The accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of petitioner as he drove his vehicle at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and without observing movement of vehicles on the road.
The petitioner drove his vehicle negligently without maintaining safe distance and same has resulted in cause of accident.
There is no rashness or negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:

sentences.text: Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 03.07.2022 at about 09.05 a.m., on Hosur Main Road, near Singasandra Bus Stop, Bengaluru City, when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-05-LB- 6035, due to the rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA- 04-B-4346 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1, got examined Dr.Ramesh.B., Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.2 and MRO of Kauvery Hospital got examined as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to 17 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its State Head Legal Claims as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & Ex.R.2 and closed his side of evidence.

7. Heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

The petitioner contended that on 03.07.2022 at about 09.05 a.m., accident occurred on Hosur Main Road, near Singasandra Bus Stop, Bengaluru City, when he was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-05-LB-6035, due to the rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-04-B- 4346 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-04-B-4346 by its driver, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of canter by its driver the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross- examination of PW.1 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.

sentences.text: Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1, first information statement.
On perusal of Ex.P.1 first information, it discloses that the petitioner has lodged complaint with police on 04.07.2022 with respect to the accident occurred on 03.07.2022.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

The petitioner also furnished spot sketch,
which is marked as Ex.P.5.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
Ex.P.3 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC and U/s.185 of M.V.Act.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.4, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-04-B-4346 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.

4 i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries sustained, petitioner has produced Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.3,
wherein it discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.6 & 7 - Discharge Summaries issued by Kauvery Hospital and United Hospital, which discloses the aspect of treatment availed by petitioner at the hospital.

The petitioner examined Dr.Ramesh.B as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.11 & 12.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and assessed the right lower limb at 50% and to the whole body at 25%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at the Hospital towards which he stated to have sustained expenses.

The petitioner has produced medical bills amounting to .58,873/-
marked at Ex.P.10 & .600/- marked at Ex.P.10(a) and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.9 and 9(a).
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also,
nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.

So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .59,473/-
appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 03.07.2022 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner has been admitted as an inpatient at Hospital as he has sustained injuries.
So, during the time of treatment, the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.6 & 7 - Discharge Summaries, wherein it discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 03.07.2022 to 06.07.2022 and again from 16.07.2023 to 18.07.2023 i.e., for a period of 07 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 07 days to a sum of .3,500/-
appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:
The petitioner is the resident of Tech City Layout, Dodda Thoguru, Bengaluru and he has been admitted to hospital for treatment.
In order to prove the said aspect, the petitioner has produced Discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.6 & 7.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses towards conveyance during the period of treatment.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:

sentences.text: The petitioner contended that he was working at Broad Com Company at Wipro Campus, Electronic City, Bengaluru as a Technician and earning a sum of .1,10,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
The petitioner has not furnished any materials to show that he was earning .1,10,000/- per month.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner in order to substantiate his contention related to his occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .15,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement.

The petitioner got examined Dr.Ramesh.B, working as an Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained injuries Like Medial Malleolus fracture of right and tibia shaft fracture of right and underwent internal fixation of right medial malleolus and shaft of tibia later underwent removal of implants and later discharged.

The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the permanent residual physical disability to the right lower limb at 50%
and to the whole body at 25%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.11 & 12 i.e., OPD Card and X-ray.

PW.2 in his chief examination deposed that petitioner complains of pain in right ankle, difficulty to squat on floor sit cross legged, climb upstairs, walk on slope kneel stand on affected limb difficulty to do routine activities.
Further on examination found post right polio residual paralysis of right lower limb, difficulty to squat on floor climb upstairs walk on slope kneel sit cross legged stand on affected limb ablution.
The materials on record disclose that prior to the accident, the petitioner is affected with polio pertaining to the limb that has been injured in the accident.
PW.2 stated the said aspect in the cross examination.
PW.2 stated in the cross examination that the petitioner was having polio to the limbs which got injured in the accident.
The petitioner is not stated to be under treatment and the implants are stated to have been removed.

Further, PW.2 deposed that the difficulties stated by him include difficulties arisen from the accidental injuries as well as difficulties existed prior to the accident due to polio and they could not be assessed separately.
The disability assessed by the doctor includes impact of accident as well as polio and said aspect has been stated by PW.2 in the cross examination.
PW.2 clearly stated in the cross examination that the disability due to accidental injuries and due to polio could not be assessed separately.
The limbs that got affected due to polio are stated to have been injured in the accident.

The accidental injuries were caused to the limbs of petitioner which have been Manjunath.J vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3563381/
6 affected by polio.

sentences.text: The doctor assessing the disability stated that the disability caused due to polio and accidental injuries cannot be bifurcated and assessed separately.
The disability assessed by the doctor includes disability caused due to polio as well as accidental injuries.
PW.2 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do his routine activities, which he has been carrying prior to accident, in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The petitioner appears to have been affected by polio prior to the accident and he was stated to be performing his activities under disability caused to limbs due to polio.
Further petitioner also examined MRO at Kauvery Hospital as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 to 17 i.e., Authorization letter, police intimation, MLC and case sheets.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
The disability caused to the petitioner due to accident and due to polio cannot be bifurcated and assessed separately.

As such, as per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability caused due to impact of accident is assessed at 10%.

sentences.text: 16. The petitioner filed the petition against the respondents seeking for compensation.

Respondent No.1 specifically contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and as such, they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner since there is violation of terms of policy.
Further, the counsel for respondent No.1 argued that the accident in question occurred subsequent to the date of amendment and as such, the concept of pay and recover is also not applicable.
In order to substantiate the contention, respondent No.1 relied on the entries in the charge sheet.
The final report filed by the police is furnished before the Tribunal and same is marked as Ex.P.4.

It is mentioned that the driver of the offending vehicle was under the Manjunath.J vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3563381/
8 influence of alcohol and relevant provision has been inserted in the final report.

sentences.text: The investigation officer has filed the final report after detailed investigation and there are allegations of driver of offending vehicle being under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.
The concerned police have inserted Section 185 of IMV Act in the final report which indicates that the driver of offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.
17. Section 150(2) of IMV Act provides the defences available to the insurance company in a claim petition.
As per Section 150(2)(a)(ii) of IMV Act, driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs as laid down in Section 185 of IMV Act, is considered to be a breach of conditions of policy.
As per the materials on record, the driver of offending vehicle appears to be under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident which aspect could be depicted from the recitals of final report.
The petitioners or respondent No.2 not placed satisfactory materials in order to controvert the recitals of final report.
Respondent No.2 not appeared before the Tribunal in order to controvert the contention of either petitioner or respondent No.1.
The contention of respondent No.1 that the driver of offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident is substantiated by the recitals in the final report.
In the final report, it is clearly mentioned that the driver of offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and driven the vehicle under the influence of alcohol.
The relevant penal provision has been inserted in the final report which indicates that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.

The said aspect is considered to be violation of terms and conditions of the policy of insurance and Section 150(2)(a)(ii) of IMV Act also provides the same to be a violation of condition of the policy.

18. Further, learned counsel for Respondent No.1 argued that after the Amendment to Motor Vehicles Act (2022) w.e.f., 01.04.2022, no liability can be fastened on Insurance Company to pay compensation for violation of policy condition and order for pay and recovery also cannot be passed.
The learned counsel for Respondent No.1 referred to Section 149 of the Act prior to amendment and Section 150 of the Act post Amendment.

The accident in question occurred on 03.07.2022 i.e.,
subsequent to the amendment which came into effect from 01.04.2022.
As per Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.

In the present case, the driver of offending vehicle has driven the vehicle under the influence of alcohol which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record and same is violation of provision of IMV Act as well as terms of the policy.

The final report filed by the jurisdictional police also discloses that the driver of offending vehicle, which caused the accident, was under the influence of alcohol and appropriate penal provision is incorporated by the police in final report to that effect.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms of the policy.

Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of terms of policy, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

Further, in view of the amendment to the Act, as discussed supra, no liability can be fastened on Respondent No.1, to pay the compensation and to recover the same from the Respondent No.2 under pay and recovery theory.

19. Accordingly, the Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the liability of paying the compensation to the petitioner is to be fastened solely on the Respondent No.2, who is the owner of Manjunath.J vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3563381/
9 the offending vehicle, as he has violated the policy condition by permitting the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the same by the person who is under the influence of alcohol as on the date of the accident.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 not appeared before the Tribunal in order to controvert the contention of petitioner as well as respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the vehicle involved in the accident was taken without his permission or knowledge.
Respondent No.2 not appeared before the court and also not put forth any contention contrary to the version of petitioner and respondent No.1.

No materials are placed by respondent No.1 to show that he was not having knowledge about the driver of offending vehicle under the influence of alcohol or the aspect of alcohol consumption by the driver was concealed from him.
Respondent No.2 neither put forth any contentions nor placed any satisfactory materials in that regard.
The final report filed by the police also indicates the aspect of driver of the offending vehicle under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.
There is violation of terms of the policy issued by respondent No.1.
As there is violation of terms of the policy, the liability cannot be fastened on respondent No.1 to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .4,04,773/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Four Thousand Seven Hundred and Seventy Three only) with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
This petition against the Respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.
Respondent No.2 being the owner is solely liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest within two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.

Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Canter by its driver.
The respondent No.2, being the owner and knowing that the driver was under intoxicated state, allowed the vehicle to be driven by him at public place and as such, violated the terms of the policy as well as M.V rules.
The petitioner was also negligent and he was driving the vehicle without valid and effective licence at the time of accident.
The accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of petitioner as he drove his vehicle at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and without observing movement of vehicles on the road.
The petitioner drove his vehicle negligently without maintaining safe distance and same has resulted in cause of accident.
There is no rashness or negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:

5
The disability assessed by the doctor includes disability caused due to polio as well as accidental injuries.
The disability caused to the petitioner due to accident and due to polio cannot be bifurcated and assessed separately.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to the age.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
The contention of respondent No.1 that the driver of offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident is substantiated by the recitals in the final report.
In the final report, it is clearly mentioned that the driver of offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and driven the vehicle under the influence of alcohol.
The relevant penal provision has been inserted in the final report which indicates that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.
As per Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.
In the present case, the driver of offending vehicle has driven the vehicle under the influence of alcohol which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record and same is violation of provision of IMV Act as well as terms of the policy.
The final report filed by the jurisdictional police also discloses that the driver of offending vehicle, which caused the accident, was under the influence of alcohol and appropriate penal provision is incorporated by the police in final report to that effect.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms of the policy.
Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of terms of policy, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.
19. Accordingly, the Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the liability of paying the compensation to the petitioner is to be fastened solely on the Respondent No.2, who is the owner of Manjunath.J vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3563381/
9 the offending vehicle, as he has violated the policy condition by permitting the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the same by the person who is under the influence of alcohol as on the date of the accident.
Respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the vehicle involved in the accident was taken without his permission or knowledge.
No materials are placed by respondent No.1 to show that he was not having knowledge about the driver of offending vehicle under the influence of alcohol or the aspect of alcohol consumption by the driver was concealed from him.
